clue.text: Cakes — of soap?

parts.note: soap comes in cakes and is used in the tub, so cakes fit for a tub would be named after the place where you wash

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether some cakes are really bars of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH BUNS are sweet currant buns from the city of Bath; the clue pretends they are cakes of soap for the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath buns are sugary, fruited yeast buns, a kind of small sweet cake.

clue.text: Pet to which pater's purse was averse

definitions.text: Pet to which pater's purse was averse

parts.words: Pet to which pater's purse was averse
parts.note: a child's word for a dog, an animal Father would not pay for, with 'averse' sounding like a verse of nursery talk

explanation.surface: A family animal that Father's budget would not stretch to.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery word for a dog is the pet a child begs for and a thrifty father refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-wow is baby talk for a dog, imitating its bark, and dogs are household companions.

clue.text: Where little Arthur turns teetotal or I get a dish of spaghetti ?

definitions.text: Where little Arthur turns teetotal or I get a dish of spaghetti ?

indicators.note: turns means the short name for Arthur is read backwards

parts.note: ART is a shortened form of the name Arthur

explanation.surface: In an Italian eatery, young Arthur gives up drink while the speaker orders pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the short name; 'teetotal' is the usual crossword abbreviation. Read whole, the clue also pictures the Italian restaurant itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant serving pasta dishes.

clue.text: Acts so as to be with people of property

parts.note: the haves are the wealthy, as in 'the haves and have-nots'

explanation.surface: Someone behaves in a way that lets them mix with wealthy landowners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the haves' is a set phrase for those with wealth, contrasted with the have-nots.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to conduct oneself, to act in a certain way.

clue.text: Spies break ranks

indicators.note: break means the word ranks is smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Secret agents fall out of military formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges RANKS. NARK is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narks are informers, people who spy for the police.

clue.text: One OT book in three's revised

indicators.note: revised means the letters of three's are edited into a new order

parts.note: the word with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A Bible scholar notes that one Old Testament book appears among three that have been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges THREES, the S of the 's included, giving the book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Esther is one of the books of the Old Testament (OT).

clue.text: Such chips pa cooked, being versed by a woman

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of chips pa are fried up into a new order

explanation.surface: Father fries chips while a woman writes poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CHIPSPA. The definition plays on Sappho, the poet of Lesbos, whose verse form bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphic verse is the metre used by Sappho, the Greek poetess, so it is poetry composed by a female writer.

clue.text: Takes notice he has hurt Desmond

indicators.note: hurt means the short name for Desmond is damaged into a new order

parts.note: DES is a short form of the name Desmond

explanation.surface: Someone pays attention when a man has injured his friend Desmond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' acts on the nickname, not on the full name Desmond, scrambling its three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention, so 'heeds' matches 'takes notice'.

clue.text: As concerns Susan Sempstress as defendant

parts.note: RE means regarding or concerning
the music-hall song 'Sister Susie's Sewing Shirts for Soldiers' made Susie the famous seamstress, a sibling

explanation.surface: A legal note about a dressmaker named Susan appearing as the accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defendant' is not the accused in court but one who defends, who fights back.
explanation.definitionFit: One who resists defends themself, so a defendant here is someone holding out against attack.

clue.text: Notes the succession when the chord is loosed ?

definitions.text: Notes the succession when the chord is loosed ?

parts.words: Notes the succession when the chord is loosed ?
parts.note: a chord broken up so its notes are played one after another rather than together

explanation.surface: Someone records what follows when a bowstring is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chord' is the musical one, not a cord; loosed means broken into single notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a broken chord, its pitches sounded in rapid sequence.

clue.text: Futurologists in our climate of depression

definitions.text: Futurologists in our climate of depression

parts.words: Futurologists in our climate of depression
parts.note: people who foretell the future in a gloomy era are really those forecasting low-pressure systems in a rainy country

explanation.surface: Pundits predicting the future in an age of national gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' is not economic gloom but a meteorological low, and 'climate' is literal: forecasters in Britain's wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Forecasters of the coming weather are seers of a sort, predicting what lies ahead.

clue.text: Notes fall — hail to the south

parts.note: October is an autumn (fall) month, abbreviated OCT
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Musical notes come down as hail drives in from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' is not a verb but the American word for autumn, standing for its month OCT.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a span of eight notes in music, and the plural matches 'Notes'.

clue.text: Diana's domain

parts.note: the Roman goddess Diana, Artemis to the Greeks, had her great temple in an ancient Ionian city

explanation.surface: The territory belonging to a woman called Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: Acts 19 records the cry 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians': her temple there was one of the Seven Wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus held the famous Temple of Artemis, called Diana in the Bible, so the city was the goddess's seat.

clue.text: The British rail as I cast for fish in Norwegian waters

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British Railways, the national railway
to cast is to throw, which is to sling

explanation.surface: Britons complain while the speaker goes angling in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like a verb (to complain) but joins 'British' as the railway, BR.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisling are small sprats caught and canned in Norway, a species of little herring-like sea creature.

clue.text: Places oxen or choristers here

definitions.meaning: cattle stand ... in a byre and singers sit in the choir stalls of a church, so both are ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: IN STALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to set something in position, and the compartments where cattle and church singers are found.

clue.text: Boat from New Zealand leaving old Rhine city

indicators.note: leaving means the New Zealand abbreviation departs from the city's name

parts.note: Coblenz is the old spelling of Koblenz, a city on the Rhine

explanation.surface: A vessel sails from New Zealand, having left an old German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes NZ from COBLENZ, the older English spelling of Koblenz.
explanation.definitionFit: A coble is a flat-bottomed fishing vessel of north-east England.

clue.text: Tommy welcomed to quarters? On the contrary

definitions.text: Tommy welcomed to quarters? On the contrary

parts.words: Tommy welcomed to quarters? On the contrary
parts.note: a soldier housed in military lodgings, and also the opposite of welcomed: jeered at

explanation.surface: A soldier is shown to his lodgings, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy (Atkins) is a British private. The word means both quartered in army lodgings and jeered by a crowd, the contrary of welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracked means lodged in soldiers' quarters, and also heckled, the reverse of a warm greeting.

clue.text: Unhushably she's champed-is to be avoided

indicators.note: unhushably means the hushing sound, the shh call for silence, is dropped

parts.note: the word as written, apostrophe dropped
to champ is to munch noisily, to chew

explanation.surface: A woman chomps loudly, which is something to steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhushably' is coined: without the hushing 'sh', so that pair leaves the pronoun-plus-'s, and 'champed' supplies the munching.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to shun or abstain from, so eschewed means kept clear of.

clue.text: Rifles with fixed bayonets for marksmen?

definitions.meaning: guns with blades fitted are pointed, keen-edged firearms
skilled riflemen who hit what they aim at

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase: shooters (guns) that are sharp (bladed).
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: guns made keen-edged by blades, and expert shots who aim with deadly accuracy.

clue.text: Boarding-house providing a kind of income

definitions.meaning: a continental guesthouse where lodgers take meals

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a French-style lodging house with meals, and the money paid to someone after they stop work.

clue.text: See 18
With a list ? More than one for this sport

definitions.meaning: leaning over, as a ship lists

definitions.text: More than one for this sport
definitions.meaning: the lists, plural, were the arena for jousting on horseback

explanation.walkthrough: A ship has a list when it leans; the lists were the enclosed ground where knights jousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: leaning to one side, and jousting with lances, held in the lists.

clue.text: Cuts the odd verses

indicators.note: odd means the letters of verses are put in a strange, irregular order

explanation.surface: A poet trims the stranger lines of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges VERSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut through, so severs means cuts.

clue.text: How's she whom three realms obey? Gone west, glory be

indicators.note: gone means the compass letter has departed from the question

parts.note: the word as written, with the apostrophe dropped
W is the compass abbreviation for west
Pope's Rape of the Lock calls Queen Anne 'Great Anna! whom three realms obey'

explanation.surface: A question after the health of a monarch who ruled three kingdoms, then news of her death and a cry of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone west' looks like a euphemism for dying, but it removes W from HOWS ANNA. The three realms were England, Scotland and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a shout of praise to God, an exclamation like 'glory be'.

clue.text: Ropy bed-linen

definitions.meaning: on a sailing ship this is a rope controlling a sail
a large cloth spread on a bed

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is nautical: a sail is trimmed by a line of that name. 'Ropy' stands as 'a rope'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a line attached to a sail's corner, and a cloth covering a mattress.

clue.text: The art of "a thing of shreds and patches "?

definitions.text: The art of "a thing of shreds and patches

parts.words: The art of "a thing of shreds and patches
parts.note: the quotation, from Hamlet and Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado, describes a picture made of pasted scraps

explanation.surface: A question about the craft behind a ragged minstrel in an operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado, Nanki-Poo sings 'A wandering minstrel I, a thing of shreds and patches'; here the phrase describes pasted-together artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Collage is the art form of gluing fragments of paper and cloth onto a surface.

clue.text: "In the soup "? Not when in the this, surely

definitions.text: "In the soup "? Not when in the this, surely

parts.words: "In the soup "? Not when in the this, surely
parts.note: being in the soup means in trouble; the opposite idiom, out of danger, is also a kind of thin soup

explanation.surface: A query whether someone is in trouble, answered that they cannot be while safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is slang for in trouble; someone 'in the clear' is safe, yet clear is also a type of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear soup is consommé, and 'in the clear' means free of trouble.

clue.text: Junior town crier on, and in, night shift

definitions.text: Junior town crier on, and in, night shift

parts.words: Junior town crier on, and in, night shift
parts.note: the nursery rhyme boy runs through the town in his nightgown, crying at the windows that children should be in bed

explanation.surface: A young official who calls out news through the streets during the night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'night shift' is a nightgown, not working hours: the rhyme's boy runs 'upstairs and downstairs in his nightgown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee Willie Winkie is the little boy in the Scottish nursery rhyme who calls through the town at bedtime.

clue.text: Agreeing when and where journeys end '

definitions.text: Agreeing when and where journeys end

parts.words: Agreeing when and where journeys end
parts.note: Twelfth Night's song says 'Journeys end in lovers meeting', so settling a time and place for that meeting

explanation.surface: Fixing the time and place at which travels finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Feste's song in Twelfth Night: 'Journeys end in lovers meeting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting couples arrange to meet at a set time and place, which is going out together.

clue.text: Lots of soldiers may be such big dears

indicators.note: may be such means the letters of big dears could be rearranged into the soldiers

explanation.surface: Many troops may prove to be lovable darlings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be such' rearranges BIG DEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a large army unit, so several of them make many troops.
